speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are here for sudden-onset vertigo; to help me narrow this down, have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or hearing changes like ringing in your ears alongside the spinning sensation?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). The clinical presentation of a sudden, brief (3-minute) episode of vertigo occurring while lying down, followed by immediate resolution and the absence of auditory symptoms or neurological deficits, is classic for BPPV. I recommend a Dix-Hallpike maneuver to confirm.
